hints: Notice the column headings increase in wavelength from $10^{-10} \text{ m}$ on the left to $10^{-2} \text{ m}$ on the right.
Recall the electromagnetic spectrum in order of increasing wavelength: X-rays, then ultraviolet, then visible light, then infrared, then microwaves.
Check which row places atomic-scale $10^{-10} \text{ m}$ waves before $10^{-8} \text{ m}$ ultraviolet and centimetre-scale $10^{-2} \text{ m}$ waves last.
walkthrough: Identify the given information: four wavelengths $10^{-10} \text{ m}$, $10^{-8} \text{ m}$, $10^{-5} \text{ m}$ and $10^{-2} \text{ m}$ in order of increasing wavelength.
State the physical order: for these four regions, increasing wavelength goes X-rays, then ultraviolet, then infrared, then microwaves.
Match each value: $10^{-10} \text{ m}$ is X-ray scale, $10^{-8} \text{ m}$ is ultraviolet scale, $10^{-5} \text{ m}$ is infrared scale, and $10^{-2} \text{ m}$ is microwave scale.
Compare with the table: only the row X-rays, ultraviolet, infrared, microwaves follows increasing wavelength correctly.

A.explanation: Microwaves do not have wavelength $10^{-10} \text{ m}$ and infrared does not have wavelength $10^{-2} \text{ m}$ in this order; the row reverses short and long wavelength regions.

B.explanation: Infrared is near $10^{-5} \text{ m}$, not $10^{-10} \text{ m}$, and X-rays are near $10^{-10} \text{ m}$, not $10^{-5} \text{ m}$.

C.explanation: This row puts longest-wavelength microwaves at shortest wavelength $10^{-10} \text{ m}$ and shortest-wavelength X-rays at longest wavelength $10^{-2} \text{ m}$.

D.explanation: Wavelength increases from X-rays to ultraviolet to infrared to microwaves, matching $10^{-10} \text{ m}$ to $10^{-2} \text{ m}$.
